candidate.name: LadderSym CocoChorales-E prompted
candidate.inputContract: whole performance audio plus whole reference-score audio plus symbolic score MIDI prompt

compatibilityNotes: The repository requirement pretty-midi 0.2.9 is incompatible with NumPy 1.26 because it still uses np.int; the isolated diagnostic environment used pretty-midi 0.2.10.
The machine-wide transformers 4.57.6 changed the T5 cache API and failed before prediction; the isolated diagnostic environment used transformers 4.40.1.

The repository inference entrypoint omitted the seed call used by training while randomly reordering simultaneous symbolic-prompt tokens. The diagnostic entrypoint fixed NumPy and Torch seeds from cfg.seed before inference.

evaluationAdapter.alignment: fixed monotonic edit-distance alignment of missing+correct semantic notes to every score position
evaluationAdapter.extraAssignment: every extra semantic note assigned to the nearest aligned score position by a fixed time-plus-pitch cost; an all-extra output falls back to monotonic full-score alignment
evaluationAdapter.mergedSubstitution: missing target plus a same-position extra note one or two semitones from the target
evaluationAdapter.drag: always false because the checkpoint has no duration-error class
evaluationAdapter.falsePositiveAccounting: predictions on ordinary-correct positions count as strict false positives; predictions on another known positive gate are reported as off-scope and excluded from FP, matching the existing Round 5 refinement accounting

experiments.reference: MuseScore render and MIDI from the authoritative MusicXML; performance/reference duration ratio 1.22x to 1.68x
same standard score render; independent fixed prompt-order seed
violin score MIDI locally warped to the existing score-alignment note timeline, then rendered and duration-corrected without reading Round 5 truth labels

reproducibility.crossSeedStableConclusionMeaning: Both fixed seeds fail every frozen gate with catastrophic strict false positives; individual semantic-track collapse patterns vary with prompt token order.

reasons: No gate passes precision >= 0.90, recall >= 0.50, and strict FP = 0.
Both standard-reference seeds produce more than 50 fresh strict false positives for missing and extra.
Local score-time alignment does not rescue the result.
The checkpoint cannot represent the project drag gate.
Semantic-track collapse depends on symbolic prompt token ordering even though the fail decision is stable.

conclusion.direction: The score-conditioned architecture class remains relevant, but this public checkpoint is not a safe violin detector. Continue with signed real note-level training data and untouched Round 6 rather than integrating LadderSym.
